subject: Recap & Action: SDK auth, structured output, embeddings, and VPC onramp for CloudStride
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Mills <ava.mills@cloudstride.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & Action: SDK auth, structured output, embeddings, and VPC onramp for CloudStride

Hi Ava — great demo earlier. Thanks for the time and for walking through your primary production constraints (HIPAA-adjacent data controls, predictable tail latency for embeddings, and the multi-tenant ingestion pipeline). Pulling together the immediate next steps we discussed so the engineers have a single checklist: 

1) Networking & private connectivity
   - Preferred: VPC endpoint to Redwood Private control plane + egress via CloudStride NAT with an allowlist of Redwood egress IPs.
   - Fallback: public egress with per-request client token + IP allowlist on your firewall.
   - Action: infra@cloudstride.com to confirm whether a managed VPC endpoint (AWS VPC Endpoint / Azure Private Link) is acceptable.

2) SDK & auth options
   - Options: short-lived API keys (recommended for hosted Dedicated) OR mutual TLS between your service and Redwood edge (required for air-gapped/regulated tenants).
   - We attached an "SDK auth matrix" showing trade-offs and sample env vars.

3) Routing & structured output/tool-calling
   - If you plan to use structured tool-calls (function calling), we recommend routing those requests to our private tier to avoid throttling.
   - Provide a sample schema for the actions you need (we can map to Redwood structured output validation).

4) Embeddings & reranking
   - For your vector store cadence, we propose batched embedding jobs (prefetch + KV-cache friendly) and a lightweight reranker model for candidate narrowing.
   - Marcus will share throughput targets so we can size Dedicated pools.

5) Security/compliance "Evidence"
   - You asked about audit logs and KMS integration — we support customer-managed KMS and token audit trails.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_auth_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), cloudstride-mutual-action-plan.pdf (MAP draft)

Proposed timeline: tech deep-dive with infra & security next Tue/Thu — can you share availability?

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Ava Mills <ava.mills@cloudstride.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: infra@cloudstride.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & Action: SDK auth, structured output, embeddings, and VPC onramp for CloudStride

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from infra/security after our quick sync: 

- For VPC endpoint, we prefer PrivateLink (AWS). We'll need the service name and any required IAM policy templates.
- Egress: we operate egress through a centralized NAT; can you provide the exact CIDR(s) / IP ranges we should allow? We need those to complete firewall rules.
- mTLS: security wants a short note on cert rotation and whether Redwood can integrate with our internal CA or if we need to use your managed certs.
- Embeddings SLA: can you propose a P95 latency target for 512-token inputs and a cost estimate based on 1M embeddings/month?

We'll block time for a 60-minute technical deep-dive Wednesday 20th at 10:00 PT if that works for your team.

Ava Mills
Director of Product Operations, CloudStride
ava.mills@cloudstride.com

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & Action: SDK auth, structured output, embeddings, and VPC onramp for CloudStride

Looping internal owners and assigning items before the Wed deep-dive: 

- Marcus: please prepare throughput/instance sizing for embeddings + proposed P95 latency for 512-token batch (include both FP16 and int8 quantized estimates). Deliverable: short slide + cost delta table. Due: Tue EOD.
- Ben: draft the PrivateLink service name template and example IAM policy. Also list our managed egress IP ranges (we have 3 /24s for the us-west region).
- Jonas: prepare sample SDK snippets for both short-lived API keys and mTLS client setup (include curl, node, and python examples). Add a small example showing structured output validation schema and a sample reranker call.
- I'll coordinate the demo environment and provision a temporary Dedicated pool for the POC.

Also note: security will ask for SOC2 evidence and a KMS integration doc; Marcus, do you have the KMS integration checklist we can surface?

Thanks — will aim to have the packet ready prior to Wed.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
VP, Solutions
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Mills <ava.mills@cloudstride.com>, infra@cloudstride.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & Action: SDK auth, structured output, embeddings, and VPC onramp for CloudStride

Hi Ava / infra team — thanks, confirmed Wed 20 Apr 2027 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive. Agenda we will cover in the 60m: 

- 5m: goals and scope (production SLOs, regulatory constraints)
- 15m: Networking plan (PrivateLink service name + egress IPs + firewall rules) — Ben will present
- 15m: Auth & SDK patterns (short-lived tokens vs mTLS + rotation + KMS) — Jonas will demo code samples
- 15m: Embeddings sizing and rerank flow (P95 targets, batching, Dedicated pool sizing) — Marcus will present
- 10m: Open questions & next steps (MAP, timelines, procurement)

Quick answers to your earlier items: 
- PrivateLink: Ben attached the service-name template in our internal packet; if you prefer, we'll provide a CloudFormation snippet during the call.
- Egress IPs: for us-west Dedicated/test pool the current public egress ranges are: 34.204.120.0/24, 34.204.121.0/24, 34.204.122.0/24. We'll confirm these in the deck.
- mTLS: Redwood supports both managed certs and customer-supplied certs via our KMS/HSM integrations. Rotation can be automated via our control plane; we'll include a short note on renewal windows and trust anchors.
- Embeddings P95: preliminary target is <120ms for single 512-token embedding on a Dedicated fp16 worker; Marcus will provide a conservative estimate with quantization tradeoffs.

I'll attach the meeting invite and the MAP in follow-up. See you Wed.

Best,
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
